ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a blue square wave drawn on a gray oscilloscope-style grid. The waveform repeats regularly, with each cycle starting at a rising edge, staying high for a short interval, then staying low for the rest of the cycle until the next rising edge. Visual count from one rising edge to the next gives one full period of about 10 equal horizontal grid divisions. Within that same period, the high level lasts about 3 of those divisions. Reasoning: Duty cycle = high-time / period × 100%. Using the counted divisions, duty cycle = 3 / 10 × 100% = 30%.

raw_record.question_text: Question: Determine the duty cycle of this square wave signal, as shown in the figure. The duty cycle is ______%.

method.method_draft: From the figure, first identify one complete cycle of the square wave by locating two consecutive rising edges. Count the horizontal grid divisions over which the signal remains high within that cycle, then count the total horizontal divisions in the cycle. The high duration is about 3 divisions and the period is about 10 divisions, so compute (3/10) × 100 = 30%.
